src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60 — [P1, confidence 75, advisory] `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` publishes each transition before line 68 commits its detector state, so a state-commit failure followed by retry republishes the same logical transition; although a producer might deduplicate stable occurrence IDs, the abstract hook does not require stable IDs and status-change messages have no enforced idempotency key, so the split transaction boundary still exposes consumers to duplicate issues and notifications.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in process_detectors(), create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result) is called at line 60-61 for each result before the handler's state is committed. Looking at the diff, the state commit happens via handler.commit_state_updates() which is called elsewhere (not shown being called in process_detectors). If state commit fails after occurrences are published, a retry would republish the same occurrences. The diff shows StatusChangeMessage objects being created without idempotency keys, and the abstract build_occurrence_and_event_data hook doesn't enforce stable IDs. This is a real atomicity/idempotency concern introduced by this code structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — [P1, confidence 100] `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` leaves every abstract method unimplemented, so resolving `Detector.detector_handler` for `metric_alert_fire` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` and aborts detector processing instead of producing an occurrence.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now extends `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` with just `pass`, meaning it doesn't implement any methods. Looking at `StatefulDetectorHandler`, it has three abstract methods marked with `@abc.abstractmethod`: `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` doesn't implement these abstract methods, attempting to instantiate it (which happens in `Detector.detector_handler` property when calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. This is a real bug that would break detector processing for metric alerts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60 — [P2 advisory, confidence 50] `for result in detector_results.values(): ... create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` publishes each occurrence before line 68 commits any detector state, so a Kafka failure after an earlier item succeeds aborts the batch with partial external output and a retry republishes the earlier occurrence because its dedupe state was never committed.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at process_detectors() (lines 56-68), the code iterates through detector_results.values() and calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result) for each result before any state is committed. The commit_state_updates() is called on the handler after the loop. If Kafka publishing fails partway through the batch, some occurrences will have been published but the detector state won't be committed. On retry, the dedupe check won't prevent republishing because the dedupe state was never persisted. This is a valid atomicity/consistency concern introduced by this diff's changes to the processing flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:49 — [confidence 100][P1] The unrelated return-contract rewrite `) -> list[tuple[Detector, dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]]]:` expands a task limited to adding an occurrence-building hook and makes `process_detectors` fail with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'values'` for every existing `DetectorHandler.evaluate` implementation that still honors the prior list contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that existing DetectorHandler.evaluate implementations that return lists will cause AttributeError when process_detectors calls .values() on them. However, looking at the diff, the code at line 63 shows `for result in detector_results.values():` which would indeed fail if detector_results is a list. But examining the diff more carefully, the MockDetectorHandler in the test file is also updated to return a dict: `return {None: DetectorEvaluationResult(None, True, DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH)}`. The abstract base class DetectorHandler.evaluate is also updated to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. This is a coordinated change across the codebase - all implementations shown in the diff are updated together. The MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler which has the new dict return type. There's no evidence of existing implementations that still return lists that would break.

The diff shows this is intentional design - MetricAlertDetectorHandler is a base class that will be extended.
